title: Ambiguity with notating commands

labels.name: editorial
labels.description: Changes that do not affect how the standard is understood

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? ``: "The [code](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-code-element) element [represents](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#represents) a fragment of computer code. This could be an XML element name, a filename, a computer program, or any other string that a computer would recognize." ``: "The [kbd](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-kbd-element) element [represents](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#represents) user input (typically keyboard input, although it may also be used to represent other input, such as voice commands)." Given the above definitions, you could argue that a command could fit inside a `` or `` element depending on context; it isn't clear which one is most semantically-correct. Some cases seem unambiguous. `
`-`` blocks use `` for commands within the sample block, since a user typed those parts of the text:

```

jdoe@mowmow:~$ ssh demo.example.com
Last login: Tue Apr 12 09:10:17 2005 from mowmow.example.com on pts/1
Linux demo 2.6.10-grsec+gg3+e+fhs6b+nfs+gr0501+++p3+c4a+gr2b-reslog-v6.189 #1 SMP Tue Feb 1 11:22:36 PST 2005 i686 unknown

jdoe@demo:~$ _

```

But, what about outside of ``? If I state "The `command` command can be used to ...", then I'm not telling a user to give this input; I'm simply stating a user *could* type this (compared to "First, execute `command` ...").

1. ~~Does `` imply a user *did* type something, or does it also semantically indicate that a user *is able* to type something?~~ See the following comment for my interpretation.

2. If specified by name vs. by path, would `command` and `/bin/command` be notated differently? `` can semantically mean a filename, implying only `/bin/command` is correct, but it could be user input too.

3. If a command is using shell-specific syntax, like `command >/dev/null 2>&1` for a POSIX-compliant shell, which element is more appropriate? Perhaps both?

4. And if both `` and `` elements can be simultaneously semantically correct for a command, which element should nest which? Should it depend on context?

Apologies in advance if I've missed a document which explains this in more detail. Let me know what you think!
